record.original_question: Can the Wasserstein geometry of elliptical distributions be developed in a way analogous to the known Wasserstein geometry of Gaussian measures?

evidence.quote: Furthermore, can we study the Wasserstein geometry of elliptical distributions in the spirit of [37] (also see [40])?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Recall that the 2-Wasserstein distance between two Borel probability measures μ, ν on R^n with finite second moments is

  W_2(μ, ν)^2 = inf_{π ∈ Π(μ,ν)} ∫_{R^n × R^n} |x − y|^2 dπ(x, y),

where Π(μ, ν) denotes the set of couplings of μ and ν. The set P_2(R^n) of such measures, equipped with W_2, is a metric space (the Wasserstein space) on which a rich infinite-dimensional Riemannian-type geometry has been developed (formal Riemannian metric on tangent spaces of absolutely continuous measures, Otto calculus, geodesics given by displacement interpolation, etc.).

The subspace G(n) of nondegenerate Gaussian measures N(m, Σ) on R^n (with m ∈ R^n and Σ ∈ Sym_+^n positive definite) is a totally geodesic, finite-dimensional submanifold of P_2(R^n). On G(n), the 2-Wasserstein distance has the closed form

  W_2(N(m_1, Σ_1), N(m_2, Σ_2))^2 = |m_1 − m_2|^2 + tr(Σ_1 + Σ_2 − 2(Σ_1^{1/2} Σ_2 Σ_1^{1/2})^{1/2}),

and G(n) carries an explicit Riemannian metric (the Bures–Wasserstein metric on Sym_+^n combined with the Euclidean metric on R^n), with explicit geodesics, curvature, exponential and logarithm maps, and barycenter theory.

A probability measure μ on R^n is called elliptical with location m ∈ R^n, scatter Σ ∈ Sym_+^n, and radial generator (a probability law ρ on [0, ∞)) if μ is the law of m + Σ^{1/2} R U, where U is uniform on the unit sphere S^{n−1} and R ∼ ρ is independent of U. Fix a radial law ρ with finite second moment, and let E_ρ(n) ⊂ P_2(R^n) be the family of all elliptical distributions on R^n with this generator ρ, parametrized by (m, Σ) ∈ R^n × Sym_+^n.

Problem. Develop a Wasserstein geometry of E_ρ(n) parallel to that of the Gaussian submanifold G(n). In particular, address the following:

(i) Show that E_ρ(n) is a totally geodesic submanifold of (P_2(R^n), W_2), and identify the W_2-geodesics within E_ρ(n) explicitly in terms of (m, Σ).

(ii) Derive a closed-form expression for W_2(μ_1, μ_2) when μ_1, μ_2 ∈ E_ρ(n), as a function of (m_1, Σ_1), (m_2, Σ_2), and the moments of ρ.

(iii) Equip E_ρ(n) with the induced Riemannian metric and compute its sectional curvature, exponential and logarithm maps, and Wasserstein barycenters of finite families of elliptical measures.

(iv) Determine to what extent the Otto-type formal Riemannian structure, the displacement convexity of standard functionals (entropy, potential, interaction energies), and gradient-flow formulations on the Gaussian submanifold extend to E_ρ(n), and identify any genuinely non-Gaussian phenomena.
artifact.status_search_result: Several aspects of the proposed program are already known: the 2-Wasserstein distance between two elliptical distributions sharing the same radial generator admits a closed form involving the Bures metric on covariance matrices (analogous to the Gaussian case), and this has been used in applied work on elliptical embeddings and elliptical processes. However, a fully developed intrinsic Wasserstein-Riemannian geometry of elliptical families (curvature, barycenters, displacement convexity, Otto calculus, etc.) parallel to the Gaussian theory does not appear to be completely worked out in the literature, so the broader program is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Generalizing Point Embeddings using the Wasserstein Space of Elliptical Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: For elliptical distributions endowed with the 2-Wasserstein metric, the squared 2-Wasserstein metric has a closed form equal to a weighted sum of the squared Euclidean distance between means and the squared Bures metric between covariance matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Closed-form W_2 distance between elliptical distributions with the same generator is established.

status_evidence.title: The Spectral-Domain W_2 Wasserstein Distance for Elliptical Processes
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral-domain W_2 Wasserstein distance for elliptical processes and Gelbrich bound.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions of W_2 theory to elliptical processes have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Information geometry of Wasserstein statistics on shapes and affine deformations
status_evidence.snippet: Wasserstein statistics on shape/affine deformation families, generalizing the Gaussian Wasserstein geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Related Wasserstein-geometric frameworks for non-Gaussian families exist but a complete elliptical analogue is not fully developed.
